prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Equal standing height. Use ONLY named scene cast; never add a child to natural-subject nonfiction. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: The Red Crayon; World Discovery; fiction.
Setting: A classroom art table in daylight; Kit left, Zoe right; same two sheets throughout.
Locked recurring subjects/props: One thick red crayon; Zoe’s white sheet with a red kite; Kit’s white sheet initially blank; Two wooden clips on a low display string
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use the props' initial state; no future story events, no captions. The book's visual premise is: Kit and Zoe stand beside two clipped pictures: Zoe’s red kite and Kit’s red balloon. The single red crayon rests on the art table.

visualReview.note: Directly viewed cast/prop reference: Kit and Zoe consistent identity and clothing; red crayon, white papers, line drawings and display cord/pegs. Finished drawing motifs treated as design only, not early-page states.
visualReview.limits: Direct agent image/sequence inspection; not physical classroom observation.
